components.gap: Partial. The success condition requires the component (account for every promised proof or evidence claim in the selected extent, with the finite dependent-source set fixed) to be supplied, with empirical claims keeping their study/task/population/uncertainty and conflict boundaries. The fixed set (tab:p15-w02b-p15-022-dependent-sources) is scoped at 022 lines 668-670 and 848-849 to claims the survey reports as established elsewhere, which is narrower than every proof or evidence claim in the extent. Not accounted for anywhere on the route: (i) the survey's own empirical/historical evidence claims: that the Brier score is used in practice to score weather forecasters and political analysts (held source p. 242); that Lewis's 1994 formulation is how the Principal Principle is usually understood and that the large literature on the principle overlooks the change of formulation (p. 243); and that formal epistemology has been a leading growth area with Bayesian approaches dominant in it (p. 247). These are omitted rather than given an evidential status, so no study/task/population/uncertainty or conflict boundary is retained for them. (ii) The claim authored at rationality-4-1.tex 216-222, that the accuracy-dominance argument needs one specific strictly proper measure, depends on Bronfman (manuscript), cited on p. 242 and listed on p. 249; Bronfman does not appear in the fixed dependent-source set or anywhere in rationality-4-1.tex or the 022 chapter.

components.gap: Partial. Normalization and the multiplier equations are explained without presupposing a feasible optimizer, and the worked distributions solve their declared problems, but the component's required extent (the complete construction in the original paper, including its constraint/normalization derivations) is not supplied for the multipliers. (a) Jaynes's (2-15), the maximum-entropy estimate of the derivatives of the constraint functions with respect to external parameters, -(1/lambda_r) times the parameter derivative of ln Z (p. 623), on which the forces in (3-4) rest (p. 624), is neither stated nor derived. (b) The general small-change relations (5-1)-(5-3), which Jaynes derives by returning to the general problem of Sec. 2 and which make lambda_k the integrating factor of the generalized heat dQ_k and the quantity statistically conjugate to f_k, with lambda = dS/d<E> = 1/T in (5-8) (pp. 627-628), are absent. Neither 166.6 nor 166.7 states, under the hypotheses of thm:p15-w02b-p15-043-existence, how the maximal entropy v_nu(c) changes with the declared values (dv/dc_k = lambda_k); so the source's interpretation of the multipliers is not given and is not made conditional on its premises. Only the identification lambda_1 = 1/kT appears (043 line 484).

components.gap: Partial. The inferential interpretation is made conditional on the reconstructed premises (J1)-(J5), but these are not the paper's complete inferential argument and stated premises, which the component's required extent demands. Not reconstructed anywhere on the route (no occurrence of ergodicity, metric transitivity or equal a priori probabilities in 166.6 or 166.7): (a) the paper's thesis that statistical mechanics, read as inference, does not depend on ergodicity, metric transitivity or equal a priori probabilities (abstract p. 620; Sec. 1 p. 621; Sec. 4 p. 627; Sec. 6 p. 629), with its premise that the general laws of motion give no information about the state beyond what measurement supplied, and its argument that newly found integrals of motion, or a proof that a system is not metrically transitive, would give no rational basis for excluding states the information allows unless new data are added (pp. 624-625); (b) the normative claim that maximum-entropy estimates are justified independently of experimental verification and remain the best estimates the given information permits whether or not they agree with experiment (abstract p. 620; p. 626). Because these premises and conclusions are missing, the inferential interpretation is conditional on an incomplete statement of the source's premises.

defect_observations.observation: The face-area value 1/4 is presented as part of Hajek and Staffel's factory example; the held source (p. 244) gives only 1/2 (side) and 1/8 (volume) and says face area yields another answer. The 022 chapter (lines 383-386) cites pp. 243-244 for 1/2, 1/4 and 1/8. The 166.7 chapter (044 lines 172-174) states the attribution correctly.

The survey's general relative-entropy dynamics is left with a statement that existence and uniqueness must be established, without linking to the declared problem of 166.6 with reference measure C_old (finite case, thm:p15-w02b-p15-043-finite). That problem settles existence and uniqueness for expectation-form constraints, including a conditional-credence constraint. Not counted against C01, since a limitation is supplied.

The survey names Jaynes (2003), Probability Theory: The Logic of Science (reference list p. 249), as the advocate. The linked reconstruction in 166.6 is of Jaynes 1957. The link does not name the version difference.

The Source paragraph says Sections 1-6 and Appendix A are treated. Not reconstructed: (2-15); Section 5's (5-1)-(5-18), apart from the n. 18 rigour caveat at lines 514-517; and the ergodicity/metric-transitivity argument of pp. 620-629.

The text says (3-1)-(3-4) are recovered by identifying lambda_1 = 1/kT and the free energy. Jaynes obtains the forces in (3-4) as special cases of (2-15), which is not stated or derived in the chapter.
